content: TAF11, also referred to as TAFII28, is a protein encoded by the TAF11 gene in humans. This protein plays a critical role in the initiation of transcription by RNA polymerase II, which requires the coordinated activity of over 70 polypeptides. The protein complex that orchestrates these activities is Transcription Factor IID (TFIID). TFIID binds to the core promoter region of genes, ensuring proper positioning of RNA polymerase II. It also serves as a scaffold for the assembly of the remaining components of the transcription complex and acts as a conduit for regulatory signals. TFIID is composed of the TATA-binding protein (TBP) and a group of evolutionarily conserved proteins known as TBP-associated factors (TAFs). These TAFs contribute to basal transcription, act as coactivators, assist in promoter recognition, and modify general transcription factors (GTFs) to facilitate the assembly of the transcription complex and the initiation of transcription. The TAF11 gene encodes a small subunit of TFIID that is present in all TFIID complexes and interacts directly with TBP. Additionally, TAF11 interacts with another small subunit, TAF13, forming a heterodimer with a structure resembling the histone core. In molecular biology, TAFII28 refers to this TATA box-binding protein-associated factor. Together with TBP and other TAFs, it forms the general transcription factor TFIID, which is essential for assembling the transcription preinitiation complex. The conserved region of TAF11 is located at the C-terminus of most member proteins. The crystal structure of human TAFII28 (hTAFII28) in complex with human TAFII18 (hTAFII18) reveals that this conserved region is involved in the binding of these two subunits. This region contains four alpha helices and three loops arranged in a manner similar to histone H3. TAF11 has been shown to interact with several proteins, including: General Transcription Factor IIF subunit 1 (GTF2F1), RNA polymerase II subunit A (POLR2A), TAF13, TAF15, TATA-binding protein (TBP), and Transcription Factor IIB (TFIIB).
